**Answer: c = 1/25**

**Lower bound (construction).** Take five classes V₁,…,V₅ of size n/5 arranged in a cycle. Join consecutive classes completely, and inside each class place a triangle-free graph with independence number o(n), which contributes only o(n²) edges.

- **K₅-free:** Any clique uses at most 2 vertices from each class, since the inside graphs are triangle-free. It can span only two consecutive classes, because a C₅ blow-up has no triangles. So a clique has at most 4 vertices.
- **Small independence number:** Each class has independence number o(n), so the whole graph does too.
- **Edges that must be removed:** The graph has 5·(n/5)² = n²/5 cross edges. A maximum bipartite subgraph of a balanced C₅ blow-up keeps 4 of the 5 class-pairs, so at least (1/5)·n² /5 = n²/25 edges must be deleted, up to o(n²).

So c ≥ 1/25. Unequal class sizes x_i give min_i x_i x_{i+1} ≤ 1/25 under Σx_i = 1, so the balanced blow-up is the worst case within this family.

**Upper bound.** I did not verify that every such graph can be made bipartite by removing (1/25 + o(1))n² edges. I am relying on my recollection that this matches the known weighted Andrásfai–Erdős–Sós-type results for Ramsey–Turán problems (Lüders–Reiher). The other agent's note gives the same value, but I reached it independently only for the lower bound.

ANSWER: 1/25
